dashboard.title: Dashboard guide
dashboard.summary: Use the dashboard to spot your best next step, review progress, and jump into the pages that need attention.
dashboard.hint: Get a quick overview of what the dashboard is showing and where to click next.

focus.title: Up next
focus.description: The Up next list ranks the tasks you can start right now, favoring trader unlocks, tasks that open follow-ups, and tasks you are close to finishing.
focus.bullet_one: When nothing is available, it shows the locked tasks that are one requirement away from opening.
focus.bullet_two: If it looks wrong, check your task filters first because hidden tasks change the list.

progress.title: Progress cards
progress.description: The progress cards are shortcuts into tasks and needed items with your current totals already in context.
progress.bullet_one: Task and objective cards jump back into your quest list.
progress.bullet_two: Item cards jump straight to the matching needed-items view for tasks or hideout.

review.title: Longer-term review
review.description: Trader and milestone sections are for checking broader progression, not just your next click.
review.bullet_one: Use traders to see which quest lines still have the most work left.
review.bullet_two: Use milestones to check Kappa, Lightkeeper, and overall completion pace at a glance.

tasks.title: Tasks guide
tasks.summary: Use the tasks page to browse available work, switch perspectives, and narrow the list to exactly what you want to focus on.
tasks.hint: Get a quick explanation of task views, filters, and where the important settings live.

views.title: Pick a view
views.description: The top row changes how tasks are grouped so you can browse by list, trader, map, or graph.
views.bullet_one: List view is best for normal progression checks and quick search.
views.bullet_two: Trader, map, and graph views are better when you already know the angle you want to review.

filters.title: Trim the list
filters.description: Status tabs focus on what is available, locked, completed, or failed. The Filters button narrows tasks by type, keys, team, or map.
filters.bullet_one: Search works across task names and helps when the list feels too large.
filters.bullet_two: Active filters show as chips under the toolbar; select one to remove it, or use Clear all.

settings.title: Adjust behavior
settings.description: The Settings button opens display preferences: what task cards show, which status tabs appear, and how sorting and fail actions behave.
settings.bullet_one: Use Filters to change which tasks appear, and Settings to change how they look.
settings.bullet_two: If the page feels off, settings are the first place to check before assuming data is missing.

needed_items.title: Needed items guide
needed_items.summary: Use needed items to combine task and hideout materials, then narrow the list to the exact items you still care about.
needed_items.hint: A quick look at scopes, the Items and Needs views, and filters.

scopes.title: Choose a scope
scopes.description: Tabs at the top switch between all items, task-only, hideout-only, and completed needs.
scopes.bullet_one: Use task-only when you are questing and do not want hideout materials mixed in.
scopes.bullet_two: Use completed when you want to review what you already satisfied instead of what is still missing.

views.title: Pick a view
views.description: Items adds every quest and hideout need for an item together. Needs lists each quest objective and hideout upgrade on its own. Both come as a list or a grid.
views.bullet_one: Use Items to decide what to keep after a raid: each item shows its total and its FIR split.
views.bullet_two: Use Needs to track one objective or upgrade at a time. Every entry has the same +/- or check control.

filters.title: Refine the list
filters.description: The Filters button controls owned-item visibility, FIR rules, team needs, and Kappa-only items. Active filters show as chips under the toolbar.
filters.bullet_one: If an item disappears unexpectedly, check the filter chips; remove one to bring those items back.
filters.bullet_two: Sorting by priority is best when you want the highest-impact items first.

hideout.title: Hideout guide
hideout.summary: Use the hideout page to see what stations are ready, what is blocked, and what materials still matter for upcoming upgrades.
hideout.hint: Get a quick explanation of hideout statuses, availability rules, and where to find the linked materials.

statuses.title: Read the statuses
statuses.description: The main filters split stations into all, available, locked, and maxed so you can focus on the right stage.
statuses.bullet_one: Available is the fastest way to see what you can build right now.
statuses.bullet_two: Locked is useful when you want to understand what requirements are still missing.

requirements.title: Control blockers
requirements.description: The settings menu can enforce station, skill, and trader requirements so availability matches how strict you want the page to be.
requirements.bullet_one: Turn requirement filters on when you only want upgrades that are fully buildable right now.
requirements.bullet_two: Turn them off when you want a broader planning view of what is coming soon.

materials.title: Follow the materials
materials.description: Each station card shows the items and prerequisites behind the next upgrade, with links back to the broader item workflow.
materials.bullet_one: Use station cards when you want upgrade details without leaving the page.
materials.bullet_two: Jump to needed items when you want the full cross-station shopping list for hideout progress.

tarkovtracker_org_vs_io.overview: Use TarkovTracker.org. TarkovTracker.io is the original founder's site and has not been updated since August 2024. TarkovTracker.org is the actively maintained, open-source GNU GPLv3 continuation run by a long-time contributor and former maintainer—supporting EFT changes after 0.15, bug fixes, and new features. Follow the steps below to rebuild your progress on .org.
tarkovtracker_org_vs_io.step_1_title: Create or sign in to your TarkovTracker.org account
tarkovtracker_org_vs_io.step_1_desc: Create a TarkovTracker.org account or sign in to the account where you want to track your current wipe progress.
tarkovtracker_org_vs_io.step_2_desc: Open Get started with TarkovTracker from Help or the dashboard and choose Quick import. Paste your Tarkov.dev profile link to restore level, faction, edition, prestige, and skills.
tarkovtracker_org_vs_io.step_3_desc: Continue to the game logs step and select your EFT Logs folder or ZIP to recover quest start and completion events that are still in your local logs.
tarkovtracker_org_vs_io.step_4_desc: Review your task list and hideout, then manually check off anything your Tarkov.dev profile and local logs could not recover.
tarkovtracker_org_vs_io.step_5_desc: Open Settings → API to create a new tarkovtracker.org read-write token, and update TarkovMonitor or RatScanner to point to .org.
tarkovtracker_org_vs_io.faq_3_q: Can I import directly with my TarkovTracker.io API token?
tarkovtracker_org_vs_io.faq_3_a: No. TarkovTracker.org does not offer a direct .io token import. Instead, use the Tarkov.dev profile import and EFT game-log import in Settings → Imports, then fill in any remaining tasks or hideout stations manually.
tarkovtracker_org_vs_io.faq_5_q: Does progress sync between TarkovTracker.io and TarkovTracker.org?
tarkovtracker_org_vs_io.faq_5_a: No. The two sites use completely separate accounts and databases, so changes made on one site do not carry over to the other.
tarkovtracker_org_vs_io.faq_4_q: Does the TarkovTracker.org team run TarkovTracker.io?
tarkovtracker_org_vs_io.faq_4_a: No. The .io domain and deployment are owned and controlled by the original founder, so we cannot access or fix issues there. Because TarkovTracker.org is under active development, occasional bugs or downtime can occur—we recommend keeping occasional backups from Settings.

tarkovdev.overview: Tarkov.dev is the open-source community dataset behind items, quests, traders, hideout stations, and market prices—and the data source that keeps TarkovTracker up to date. Browse it directly as a player or pull its static JSON endpoints in your own tools.
tarkovdev.step_1_title: Look up game data on the website
tarkovdev.step_1_desc: Visit tarkov.dev to search items, check quest requirements, inspect trader inventories, and review hideout upgrades in an ad-free interface.
tarkovdev.step_2_desc: Browse available schemas at json.tarkov.dev/endpoints and query the static JSON feeds directly from your app or script—no API key or authentication is required for read queries.
tarkovdev.step_3_title: Report issues or contribute on Discord
tarkovdev.step_3_desc: Join The Hideout Discord to report stale game data, coordinate with other tool authors, or help keep the dataset accurate.
tarkovdev.tip_1: The JSON endpoints have no rate limit, but production apps should cache responses client-side to avoid redundant downloads.
tarkovdev.faq_1_q: Is the Tarkov.dev API free to use?
tarkovdev.faq_1_a: Yes. Standard read queries against the static JSON endpoints are completely free and require no account or API key.
tarkovdev.faq_2_q: How often is the data updated?
tarkovdev.faq_2_a: Community contributors update the dataset as in-game changes are discovered—often multiple times per day right after a wipe or patch.

tarkovmonitor.overview: TarkovMonitor is a desktop app by The Hideout team that watches local Escape from Tarkov log files and automatically marks completed quests in TarkovTracker. It also offers audio alerts, local raid stats, and optional Tarkov.dev integration.
tarkovmonitor.compatibility: Windows desktop app. Supports both PvP and PvE modes. Requires a TarkovTracker.org read-write API token from Settings → API.
tarkovmonitor.step_1_desc: Download the latest Windows release ZIP from the official GitHub Releases page.
tarkovmonitor.step_2_desc: Extract the archive to a permanent folder, then run TarkovMonitor.exe. Do not run it directly from inside the ZIP file.
tarkovmonitor.step_3_desc: Create a read-write API token in TarkovTracker Settings → API, then open TarkovMonitor's TarkovTracker integration settings and paste it in.
tarkovmonitor.step_4_desc: Leave TarkovMonitor running during your session. When Escape from Tarkov writes a supported quest-completion event to its logs, TarkovMonitor updates TarkovTracker automatically.
tarkovmonitor.troubleshooting_1_desc: Confirm your token has read-write permissions, has not expired, and points to TarkovTracker.org on the latest TarkovMonitor release.
tarkovmonitor.troubleshooting_2_desc: Normal monitoring only processes new log entries. Use Read Past Logs in Initial Setup and select the right wipe and profile breakpoint to backfill earlier quests.
tarkovmonitor.troubleshooting_3_desc: Match your TarkovTracker game mode setting (PvP or PvE) to the mode you are playing in-game.
tarkovmonitor.tip_1: Use Read Past Logs once during initial setup if you are starting mid-wipe and want to recover quests already recorded in local logs.
tarkovmonitor.tip_2: If you previously used TarkovTracker.io, replace your old token with a newly generated tarkovtracker.org read-write token.
tarkovmonitor.faq_1_a: TarkovMonitor only reads the log files Escape from Tarkov writes locally—it does not read game memory, and logs are not updated mid-raid. Any third-party tool carries some risk, so use it at your own discretion.
tarkovmonitor.faq_2_q: Does TarkovMonitor work with PvE mode?
tarkovmonitor.faq_2_a: Yes. Both PvP and PvE are supported as long as your TarkovTracker game mode matches the mode you are playing.
tarkovmonitor.faq_3_q: Do I need TarkovMonitor to use TarkovTracker?
tarkovmonitor.faq_3_a: No. TarkovTracker works completely with manual tracking—TarkovMonitor simply automates supported quest updates.

ratscanner.overview: RatScanner is an open-source desktop overlay that identifies Escape from Tarkov items from screen captures and displays market prices, barter uses, and quest data. It runs externally without reading game memory.
ratscanner.compatibility: Windows desktop app. Run Escape from Tarkov in borderless or windowed mode so the overlay can appear.
ratscanner.step_1_desc: Download RatScanner.zip from the official GitHub Releases page—the project website may lag behind recent releases.
ratscanner.step_2_desc: Extract the full ZIP to a permanent folder, then run RatScanner.exe. Do not launch it directly from inside the archive.
ratscanner.step_3_desc: Pick which item details to display, adjust overlay opacity, and confirm your scan hotkeys in RatScanner settings.
ratscanner.step_5_desc: Open the TarkovTracker section in RatScanner settings, switch the backend from .io to .org, and paste an API token from Settings → API.
ratscanner.step_4_desc: Name scan: open an item inspection window and click the magnifier. Icon scan: hold your configured modifier key and left-click an item.

ratscanner.troubleshooting_2_desc: Ensure the item inspection UI is fully visible and unobstructed, then retry name scanning or icon scanning with your configured modifier.
ratscanner.troubleshooting_3_desc: Switch Escape from Tarkov from exclusive fullscreen to borderless or windowed mode.
ratscanner.troubleshooting_4_desc: RatScanner pulls market pricing from a third-party feed, so displayed values can lag behind live flea-market changes.
ratscanner.tip_1: Keep RatScanner updated from GitHub Releases—the TarkovTracker.org team helps maintain it and continues improving .org defaults.
ratscanner.tip_2: Pair RatScanner with TarkovTracker's Needed Items page for a complete checklist of every item your active quests and hideout upgrades need.
ratscanner.faq_1_a: RatScanner reads item tooltips via screen capture and does not modify the game client or interact with game servers. Battlestate Games' stance on third-party tools can change, so use it at your own risk.
ratscanner.faq_2_q: Does RatScanner work with the flea market?
ratscanner.faq_2_a: Yes. It displays current flea-market prices alongside trader values so you can compare sell options quickly.
ratscanner.faq_4_q: How does RatScanner work with TarkovTracker.org?
ratscanner.faq_4_a: Switch the TarkovTracker backend from .io to .org in RatScanner's settings and enter your tarkovtracker.org API token (Step 4). For a full view of everything your quests and hideout still require, check the Needed Items page.

account_retention.scope: These rules apply to routine account deletion for inactivity while TarkovTracker operates. They define when an account may become eligible for cleanup, not a scheduled deletion date.
account_retention.standard: No qualifying support: an account may be deleted after six consecutive months without recorded account activity.
account_retention.previous_supporter: Previous supporter: an account with a qualifying contribution recorded against it, including a one-time contribution or previous subscription, may become eligible for deletion one year after the later of its last recorded account activity and its most recent recorded contribution.
account_retention.active_subscriber: Active qualifying subscription: an account is exempt from routine inactivity deletion while its supporter subscription remains active, even if the account is not used.
account_retention.subscription_end: Canceling renewal does not end this exemption while paid subscription access continues. After subscription access ends, including any billing grace period we grant, an account becomes eligible for inactivity deletion no earlier than one year after the later of its last recorded activity and the end of its most recent subscription access period.
account_retention.activity: We assess inactivity using available records of sign-ins, authenticated site or API use, and saved account-data changes. Viewing a public profile without signing in does not count as activity for that account.
account_retention.exceptions: Fully refunded contributions do not qualify for supporter retention; other valid contributions may still qualify. A chargeback immediately removes all supporter benefits and supporter retention history, including benefits from earlier contributions. Accounts with a chargeback follow the standard six-month inactivity rule. These protections apply only to routine inactivity cleanup. They do not prevent deletion you request, action for abuse or security reasons, deletion required by law, or deletion when the Service is discontinued.
account_retention.no_guarantee: Supporting TarkovTracker does not purchase permanent storage, a backup service, or guaranteed availability or recovery. Data may be lost through failures, security incidents, or third-party outages, and the Service may be suspended or shut down. The retention policy does not guarantee that data will remain available for any particular period.
account_retention.backup: Export your progress from Settings and keep your own backup. Export and recovery may be unavailable during an outage or after data is lost or deleted.
account_retention.rights: Nothing in this policy excludes or limits rights or remedies that cannot lawfully be excluded or limited.
account_retention.notice: Where feasible, we will make reasonable efforts to notify affected users before routine inactivity deletion. Material changes to this policy will be communicated in accordance with the Terms of Service and applicable law.
account_retention.terms_summary: Routine inactivity cleanup follows the account-retention rules in Section 7.3, including the exemption for active subscribers and the one-year window for previous supporters.
account_retention.perk_summary: Protection from routine inactivity deletion under the account-retention rules in Section 7.3, including one-time contributors and previous subscribers
account_retention.liability: Any exclusion or limitation of liability for data loss or privacy-related incidents applies only to the extent permitted by applicable law. Nothing in this Policy excludes or limits rights or remedies that cannot lawfully be excluded or limited.
